ku.description: Ku (PP_3255) is the prokaryotic DNA-end binding factor of Pseudomonas putida KT2440. Its conserved Ku architecture and curated HAMAP classification support a homodimer that recognizes exposed double-stranded DNA ends and recruits and stimulates the LigD repair enzyme. These molecular properties are inferred from family conservation and characterized bacterial Ku proteins. Native KT2440 genetics shows a locus-dependent contribution to mutagenic repair of Cas9-induced breaks; some end-joining events persist without Ku or LigD. Ku also influences mutation spectra during carbon starvation in P. putida.

ligD.description: LigD (PP_3260) is a predicted multifunctional DNA end-processing and ATP-dependent ligation enzyme of Pseudomonas putida KT2440. Conserved ligase, polymerase and phosphoesterase domains support repair of broken DNA ends through the activities characterized in bacterial LigD orthologs. In native KT2440, changing LigD abundance alters Cas9-site mutation spectra, but repair persists without LigD at the loci tested. Thus LigD can contribute to mutagenic end joining without being obligatory for every repair event. Its end-processing domains also influence stationary-phase mutation spectra in P. putida.

review.summary: ATP-dependent DNA ligation is the conserved LigD catalytic role.
review.reason: Q88HU3 has LigD-specific adenylation and ligase-domain signatures. Purified Mycobacterium tuberculosis LigD ligase catalyses nick sealing, and P. aeruginosa LigD seals DNA ends in reconstitution. These support a conserved-function inference; ARBA reaction text and GO cross-references are not independent evidence. Native KT2440 catalysis and cofactor preference have not been measured here.
